html:
Huldrych Zwingli was the priest who led the Protestant Reformation in Zurich from 1519. He founded what became the Reformed churches.

He came to his ideas from reading the Bible and Erasmus, close in time to Luther but on his own path. In Zurich he preached against fasting rules, images in churches, priestly celibacy and the Mass. The city council backed him, and by 1525 Zurich had a new church order. He and Luther met at Marburg in 1529 but could not agree on the Lord's Supper.

Zwingli also preached against mercenary service. He died in battle at Kappel in 1531, fighting the Catholic cantons. The Confederacy stayed split by faith for three centuries. His work in Zurich was carried on by Heinrich Bullinger and joined with that of John Calvin in Geneva.
